strategy.summary: Regression for astropy FITS WCS API caching: with equinox undefined (NaN), the cache key in _get_components_and_classes contains NaN, so the identity cache never hits. The developer test test_components_and_classes_cache must fail on buggy 0d03eb21bfdb (world_axis_object_components not the same object on repeated access) and pass once the equinox is normalized to None when NaN. Reproduction uses the pure-Python astropy WCS API path with the project's own test file; no compiled-extension behaviour is implicated beyond the standard wcslib-backed WCS object.

pinned_because: astropy dependency is documented:false with no constraint in evidence, so no version is pinned; the buggy commit's own source tree is built instead of a released wheel so the cache code under test is the one exercised
numpy version not stated by the evidence; left unpinned and taken from the build environment

strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 0d03eb21bfdb the test FAILS: after WCS(naxis=2) with ctype RA---TAN/DEC--TAN and equinox left NaN, the two accesses to wcs.world_axis_object_components return different objects, so the identity assertion is False. On the fixed revision the cache key normalizes NaN equinox to None, the two accesses return the same cached object, and the test PASSES.
strategy.numerical_probe: Check wcs.wcs.equinox is NaN before the accesses to confirm the trigger condition is present; no numeric value is graded.

input_output_examples.input: WCS(naxis=2) with ctype RA---TAN/DEC--TAN and equinox undefined (NaN); access wcs.world_axis_object_components twice
input_output_examples.buggy_output: second access is not the same cached object (cache miss, because NaN != NaN in the cache key)

risks: Equinox is NaN only when left undefined; the passages do not cover other equinox values, so the test selects only the NaN branch.

Environment versions beyond the source tree are not stated; if the buggy-revision build is not used (e.g. a released astropy wheel is installed instead of editable build), the test may not reflect the buggy code and the transition cannot be reproduced.
Passages do not give dtype, precision, or a numeric wrong value; the failure is a cache-miss identity assertion, so manifestation is a boolean identity check rather than a numerical tolerance check.

The enclosing class name of _get_components_and_classes is not stated in the evidence; the test is planned via the public world_axis_object_components property rather than calling the private method directly.

Passing the test on the fixed revision depends on wcs.wcs.set() being called after setting ctype so the WCS is in a valid state; if the fixed revision also requires a different setup, the transition may not hold.

oracle.reference_source: developer regression test in PR astropy/astropy#20000 (identity assertion)
oracle.why: The assertion is object identity (is), a boolean property, so no numeric tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The identity assertion evaluates False on the buggy revision because the cache key contains NaN, NaN != NaN causes a cache miss, and each access rebuilds world_axis_object_components as a new object, so AssertionError is raised.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the equinox is normalized to None in the cache key, the cache hits, the same object is returned on both accesses, and the identity assertion holds.
